question.problem:
Solve the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]x(t),\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

*Hint: The only eigenvalue of the system's matrix is $\lambda =1.$*
question.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}].$

We are given that the eigenvalue is $\lambda =1$ (of multiplicity two). For this eigenvalue, we get 

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
$v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda $ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $v$, the solution to the system of differential equations is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

To find $w,$ we solve the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A-\lambda I)w & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}3-1 & 4 \\ -1 & -1-1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{w}_{1}+4{w}_{2}=-2 \\ -{w}_{1}-2{w}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the first equation is a constant multiple of the second. So, we obtain

$$
{w}_{1}=-1-2{w}_{2}.
$$

The variable ${w}_{2}$ is a free variable. Setting ${w}_{2}=0,$  we get ${w}_{1}=-1,$ and therefore

$$
w=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{t}+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Now, we need to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial condition $x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(0) & =[\begin{aligned}-2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}-([\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{t}+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2t-1){e}^{t} \\ (1-t){e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
